headline: Physical priors constrain learned models of membrane, peptide, and ligand binding
label: Physically Constrained Molecular Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and a published NTF2-fold study show explicit lipid, template, and design-scaffold priors improving prediction accuracy and small-molecule…
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the injection of explicit physical or structural information to constrain learned or computational prediction. CoMPLip places the prior at the lipid environment, co-folding membrane proteins with lipids during AlphaFold 3 prediction to form bilayer-like arrangements and improve ligand poses. PatchMAN2 places it in the template library, filtering non-productive template fragments and adding local docking modes to reduce fragment-based peptide docking runtime. The NTF2-fold study places it in the design scaffold, combining deep learning with physics-based design to yield nanomolar-to-micromolar small-molecule binders and a cortisol biosensor. What is new is locating the constraint at these levels rather than only in model architecture. The two preprints report accuracy and runtime gains, while the published work reports binder and biosensor outcomes, so the evidence base differs in kind across the set.
